stories.name: Alex Lewis
stories.headline: Strep A → septicemia, TSS & necrotizing fasciitis
stories.summary: In 2013 a mild illness became Group A Streptococcus septicemia, toxic shock syndrome, and necrotizing fasciitis. Given ~3% survival, he required quadruple amputation and facial reconstruction — including lip grafts from shoulder tissue and medical tattooing. Often confused with Staph; both can cause TSS. Documentary: The Extraordinary Case of Alex Lewis.

stories.name: Lauren Wasser
stories.headline: Menstrual TSS — tampon-associated shock & amputation
stories.summary: Model Lauren Wasser developed tampon-associated toxic shock syndrome at 24. Profound hypotension, multi-organ failure, and gangrene led to below-knee amputation and ongoing limb risk. Classic real-world anchor for menstrual TSS teaching — remove source, resuscitate, broad antibiotics, ICU.

stories.name: Aimee Copeland
stories.headline: Necrotizing fasciitis after zip-line wound
stories.summary: After a zip-line accident in 2012, Aeromonas hydrophila caused necrotizing fasciitis. She lost both hands, a leg, and a foot but survived. Useful contrast to strep-driven NF/TSS — different organism, same surgical urgency and ICU resuscitation.

stories.name: Tension pneumothorax — emergency decompression
stories.headline: Clinical recognition & needle thoracostomy
stories.summary: Emergency medicine teaching cases on tension pneumothorax: absent breath sounds, tracheal deviation, hypotension — decompress before imaging when clinically certain.

stories.name: New-onset DKA patient accounts
stories.headline: Abdominal pain masquerade + hyperglycemia
stories.summary: Patient stories of first Type 1 presentation as DKA — polyuria, abdominal pain, marked hyperglycemia — mirroring CCS cases where the surgical abdomen is a trap.

stories.name: Subdural hematoma after fall
stories.headline: Elderly fall → expanding subdural
stories.summary: Real-world accounts of chronic subdural after minor falls — fluctuating consciousness, anticoagulation risk, neurosurgical evacuation.
